answer.text: Risk-adjusted return — risk premium (portfolio return minus risk-free rate) per unit of total risk measured by standard deviation
Only the downside risk of a portfolio

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series XV (p.241), the Sharpe Ratio measures the risk premium earned per unit of standard deviation; the formula is (Portfolio Return − Risk-Free Rate) / Standard Deviation. Per p.238, standard deviation is a recognised statistical measure of total risk, which is the denominator used by Sharpe. The Trap: Sharpe uses total risk (standard deviation), not only the downside; absolute return ignores risk; correlation is a separate statistic. The keyed answer is the only one that captures both the risk-premium numerator and the standard-deviation denominator. Note: A higher Sharpe ratio indicates better risk-adjusted performance, allowing comparison of portfolios with different risk profiles.
